newsitem.title: USA: TVA sets plan to cut costs, reduce debt.
newsitem.headline: TVA sets plan to cut costs, reduce debt.

text.p: Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) said that it had set a 10-year business plan that calls for a 50 percent reduction in debt and sets a target of reducing the total cost of power 15 percent by 2007.
The business plan recommends a price increase in the 1998 fiscal year that will result in a 5.5 percent increase in its power revenues, the company said.
The plan also includes initiatives to reduce fuel, labor and supply costs, the company said, and proposes a reduction of about 725 in the workforce.

The company said the proposed price increase would result in $325 million in additional revenue. Capital expenditures would be limited to $595 million, down from a high of more than $2 billion in 1993.
It said that regular business operations along with other actions recommended by the plan are projected to increase the amount of funds for debt reduction in 1998 to $476 million.

Chief Financial Officer David Smith said in a statement, "Our goals for 2007 are to reduce the wholesale cost of power from the current 4.11 cents per kilowatt-hour to 3.46 cents, slash TVA's debt in half to $13.8 billion and respond to changing customer needs,"
"This TVA Board is the first to tackle the reduction of TVA's $27.6 billion debt. By implementing this plan, TVA can, by 2007, reduce its debt to the lowest level since 1981."
The TVA Board will consider the recommended price increase at an August 5 meeting. If approved, the increase would be effective October 1, the company said.
TVA said that electricity prices were last increased 7.8 percent in 1987.
